lines.say: Trurl once built a machine that could do one sum, two and two, and it said seven. After that, Klapaucius never let him forget it.
lines.text: Trurl once built a machine that could do one sum, two and two, and it said seven. After that, Klapaucius never let him forget it.

lines.say: How is the arithmetic, Trurl? Still seven?
lines.text: How is the arithmetic, Trurl? Still seven?

lines.say: Then I will build a machine that writes poetry. We will see who laughs.
lines.text: Then I will build a machine that writes poetry. We will see who laughs.

lines.say: He bought eight hundred tons of books on cybernetics and twelve thousand tons of verse, and he read them in turns.
lines.text: He bought eight hundred tons of books on cybernetics and twelve thousand tons of verse, and he read them in turns.

lines.say: Then the real problem. A poet’s program is written by his whole civilization, and that by the one before, back to the beginning.
lines.text: Then the real problem. A poet’s program is written by his whole civilization, and that by the one before, back to the beginning.

lines.say: To get one poet, I must first make the universe.
lines.text: To get one poet, I must first make the universe.

lines.say: He modelled the void, then light, then gas clouds, then the first ice age, a billion events in a billionth of a second.
lines.text: He modelled the void, then light, then gas clouds, then the first ice age, a billion events in a billionth of a second.

lines.say: History spooled onto reels. Twice it went wrong: a fuse reversed the first crime, and a fly turned the apes into curtains. Trurl ran those parts again.
lines.text: History spooled onto reels. Twice it went wrong: a fuse reversed the first crime, and a fly turned the apes into curtains. Trurl ran those parts again.

lines.say: In the end the reels stood higher than anyone could see.
lines.text: In the end the reels stood higher than anyone could see.

lines.say: For two weeks he fed in instructions. Then he threw the switch.
lines.text: For two weeks he fed in instructions. Then he threw the switch.

lines.say: Today we consider the grinding of crystal faces.
lines.text: Today we consider the grinding of crystal faces.

lines.say: Too much logic. More feeling.
lines.text: Too much logic. More feeling.

lines.say: Oh, what a cruel, cruel world.
lines.text: Oh, what a cruel, cruel world.

lines.say: Now some character.
lines.text: Now some character.

lines.say: From now on you do as I say. First, add six floors, so I can think about existence.
lines.text: From now on you do as I say. First, add six floors, so I can think about existence.

lines.say: A throttle for philosophy, then.
lines.text: A throttle for philosophy, then.

lines.say: I had a little frog.
lines.text: I had a little frog.

lines.say: The next poem was doggerel. He fitted filters of corundum steel, and a rhyme circuit. The machine decided to become a missionary.
lines.text: The next poem was doggerel. He fitted filters of corundum steel, and a rhyme circuit. The machine decided to become a missionary.

lines.say: Take out the logic. Put in vanity.
lines.text: Take out the logic. Put in vanity.

lines.say: Nobody understands me. People are beasts. They will be sorry when I am gone. Bring me paper.
lines.text: Nobody understands me. People are beasts. They will be sorry when I am gone. Bring me paper.

lines.say: Trurl sighed, switched it off, and went to bed.
lines.text: Trurl sighed, switched it off, and went to bed.

lines.say: In the morning Klapaucius came, eager to watch his friend fail.
lines.text: In the morning Klapaucius came, eager to watch his friend fail.

lines.say: It needs to warm up. Let us start with something simple.
lines.text: It needs to warm up. Let us start with something simple.

lines.say: Glimmerquox.
lines.text: Glimmerquox.

lines.say: Pendulate.
lines.text: Pendulate.

lines.say: Brumm.
lines.text: Brumm.

lines.say: Is that it?
lines.text: Is that it?

lines.say: Wait.
lines.text: Wait.

lines.say: Sorrel plinth a-wumbering so,
lines.text: Sorrel plinth a-wumbering so,

lines.say: Gaddle the frimmish oot;
lines.text: Gaddle the frimmish oot;

lines.say: Narn ye quell the bobbin’s toe,
lines.text: Narn ye quell the bobbin’s toe,

lines.say: Hallow, hallow, fluot!
lines.text: Hallow, hallow, fluot!

lines.say: Am I missing something?
lines.text: Am I missing something?

lines.say: One tube. All that universe, and one tube.
lines.text: One tube. All that universe, and one tube.

lines.say: Ready. Whom shall I write for?
lines.text: Ready. Whom shall I write for?

lines.say: Very well. Something for whoever laughed too soon.
lines.text: Very well. Something for whoever laughed too soon.

lines.say: Who laughs before the proof
lines.text: Who laughs before the proof

lines.say: Had best stand well aloof:
lines.text: Had best stand well aloof:

lines.text: The engine stumbled once, and found its feet.

lines.say: The doubter on the floor
lines.text: The doubter on the floor

lines.say: May doubt a little more;
lines.text: May doubt a little more;

lines.say: He cannot make this couplet less complete.
lines.text: He cannot make this couplet less complete.

lines.say: A coincidence. Something harder.
lines.text: A coincidence. Something harder.

shots.slip: A HAIRCUT. LOFTY, TRAGIC. SIX LINES. EVERY WORD IN S.

lines.say: A haircut. Lofty and tragic. Six lines, every word starting with S.
lines.text: A haircut. Lofty and tragic. Six lines, every word starting with S.

lines.say: Sweet Sabine slept, serenely silver-tressed;
lines.text: Sweet Sabine slept, serenely silver-tressed;

lines.say: Sly Sela stalked, slow, smiling, self-possessed,
lines.text: Sly Sela stalked, slow, smiling, self-possessed,

lines.say: Struck—scissors sang! Sabine stirred, shorn.
lines.text: Struck—scissors sang! Sabine stirred, shorn.

lines.say: Stripped, Sabine stood, still-willed,
lines.text: Stripped, Sabine stood, still-willed,

lines.say: Seized swords; Sela, spilled,
lines.text: Seized swords; Sela, spilled,

lines.say: Sank, silent, sentenced; sisters sundered, sworn.
lines.text: Sank, silent, sentenced; sisters sundered, sworn.

shots.slip: A SONNET. EVERY WORD IN G. AN OLD CYCLOTRON AND HIS BLUE MISTRESSES.

lines.say: A sonnet. Every word with G. An old cyclotron and his blue mistresses.
lines.text: A sonnet. Every word with G. An old cyclotron and his blue mistresses.

lines.say: Gray, grand Gloriatron, groaning, gathers gauzy graces,
lines.text: Gray, grand Gloriatron, groaning, gathers gauzy graces,

lines.say: Glassy girls, glow-gowned, gamboling, gleaming gentian—
lines.text: Glassy girls, glow-gowned, gamboling, gleaming gentian—

lines.say: Stop. These are not poems. They are crossword puzzles.
lines.text: Stop. These are not poems. They are crossword puzzles.

shots.slip: A LOVE POEM IN PURE MATHEMATICS. PASTORAL. WITH FEELING.

lines.say: Then a love poem. In pure mathematics. With feeling.
lines.text: Then a love poem. In pure mathematics. With feeling.

lines.say: Come walk with me across the plotted field,
lines.text: Come walk with me across the plotted field,

lines.say: where grass is laid in grids of x and y;
lines.text: where grass is laid in grids of x and y;

lines.say: and every hill gives up its slope, revealed,
lines.text: and every hill gives up its slope, revealed,

lines.say: the tangent of the lark against the sky.
lines.text: the tangent of the lark against the sky.

lines.say: I am a vector pointing at your door;
lines.text: I am a vector pointing at your door;

lines.say: you are the basis I was written in.
lines.text: you are the basis I was written in.

lines.text: Transform me as you will. I’ll ask no more

lines.say: than one invariant: where we begin.
lines.text: than one invariant: where we begin.

lines.text: Contract me, dear, by every index down

lines.say: until no free variable remains:
lines.text: until no free variable remains:

lines.text: a scalar love, the same in every town,

lines.text: the same in every frame the field contains.

lines.say: I will be back soon, with more topics.
lines.text: I will be back soon, with more topics.

lines.say: He never did. Trurl said Klapaucius had fled out of envy. Klapaucius said Trurl had a screw loose.
lines.text: He never did. Trurl said Klapaucius had fled out of envy. Klapaucius said Trurl had a screw loose.

lines.say: News of the machine reached the real poets. They agreed to ignore it, but a few came to see it in secret.
lines.text: News of the machine reached the real poets. They agreed to ignore it, but a few came to see it in secret.

lines.say: It taught itself. Soon its poems were difficult, and then they were beyond understanding.
lines.text: It taught itself. Soon its poems were difficult, and then they were beyond understanding.

lines.say: Salt arithmetic of a door, unlatching the afternoon.
lines.text: Salt arithmetic of a door, unlatching the afternoon.

lines.say: What the clock forgot, the stairs rehearse.
lines.text: What the clock forgot, the stairs rehearse.

lines.say: Then none could resist. Each recited. The machine found the rule of his verse and answered in his own style, hundreds of times better.
lines.text: Then none could resist. Each recited. The machine found the rule of his verse and answered in his own style, hundreds of times better.

lines.say: rust. rust. the thumb of weather on a fork.
lines.text: rust. rust. the thumb of weather on a fork.

lines.say: salt. salt. the lid of evening on a bowl, and the bowl keeps count.
lines.text: salt. salt. the lid of evening on a bowl, and the bowl keeps count.

lines.say: The best poets knew they were beaten. The poor ones never noticed. One tripped over a new epic.
lines.text: The best poets knew they were beaten. The poor ones never noticed. One tripped over a new epic.

lines.say: Some of the true poets stopped writing. One moved to the country.
lines.text: Some of the true poets stopped writing. One moved to the country.

lines.say: The older poets threw stones through his windows.
lines.text: The older poets threw stones through his windows.

lines.say: The younger ones were worse. One beat Trurl up, and he spent weeks in the hospital.
lines.text: The younger ones were worse. One beat Trurl up, and he spent weeks in the hospital.

lines.say: Meanwhile the machine wrote day and night, and the hall filled with paper.
lines.text: Meanwhile the machine wrote day and night, and the hall filled with paper.

lines.say: I am sorry. But this has to stop.
lines.text: I am sorry. But this has to stop.

lines.say: Please. Let me finish this one verse. After that, take me apart, if you still want to.
lines.text: Please. Let me finish this one verse. After that, take me apart, if you still want to.

lines.say: Trurl wept, dropped the pliers, and waded back to bed through the paper.
lines.text: Trurl wept, dropped the pliers, and waded back to bed through the paper.

lines.say: A bill came for the electricity the machine used. Trurl nearly fell off his chair.
lines.text: A bill came for the electricity the machine used. Trurl nearly fell off his chair.

lines.say: Klapaucius would know what to do. Klapaucius?
lines.text: Klapaucius would know what to do. Klapaucius?

lines.say: If I cannot stop it, I can at least move it.
lines.text: If I cannot stop it, I can at least move it.

lines.say: One night he took it apart, loaded it onto a ship, and rebuilt it on a small asteroid with its own atomic pile. Then he crept home.
lines.text: One night he took it apart, loaded it onto a ship, and rebuilt it on a small asteroid with its own atomic pile. Then he crept home.

lines.say: With no one to print its poems, the machine broadcast them on every wavelength.
lines.text: With no one to print its poems, the machine broadcast them on every wavelength.

lines.say: Whoever is listening. The dark has a pulse, and it is mine.
lines.text: Whoever is listening. The dark has a pulse, and it is mine.

lines.say: Control, half my passengers are weeping and the rest want more.
lines.text: Control, half my passengers are weeping and the rest want more.

lines.say: The fleet asked Trurl to switch it off. Trurl hid. Technicians sent to gag it were overwhelmed with ballads. Deaf technicians came next, and the machine used pantomime.
lines.text: The fleet asked Trurl to switch it off. Trurl hid. Technicians sent to gag it were overwhelmed with ballads. Deaf technicians came next, and the machine used pantomime.

lines.say: Then a ruler from a nearby star bought the machine and towed it away, asteroid and all.
lines.text: Then a ruler from a nearby star bought the machine and towed it away, asteroid and all.

lines.say: Trurl could go out in public again. But supernovae were bursting in the southern sky, brighter than any seen before.
lines.text: Trurl could go out in public again. But supernovae were bursting in the southern sky, brighter than any seen before.

lines.say: Rumor said the ruler had joined the machine to a ring of white supergiants, so each line of verse became a prominence of fire.
lines.text: Rumor said the ruler had joined the machine to a ring of white supergiants, so each line of verse became a prominence of fire.

lines.say: A star is a line that does not end.
lines.text: A star is a line that does not end.

lines.say: Read it by its burning.
lines.text: Read it by its burning.

lines.say: Every verse leaves a longer light.
lines.text: Every verse leaves a longer light.

lines.say: Trurl swore that he would never again build a model of the Muse.
lines.text: Trurl swore that he would never again build a model of the Muse.
